Construction Product Management India Manufacturing Supplier Rebar Threading Machine Buying Guide: Capacity, Thread Length, Power & Die Selection TRP Machines & Tools 11 min read · 1 hour ago -- Listen Share A rebar threading machine is an important part of a mechanical rebar splicing system. It prepares the end of a TMT/reinforcement bar so that it can connect with a compatible threaded rebar coupler . For contractors, rebar processors , fabricators and project procurement teams, selecting a machine is not simply about choosing the highest motor power or largest bar diameter. The machine should match the rebar diameter range , required thread length, thread profile , production volume, power supply, tooling and coupler system being used on the project. Press enter or click to view image in full size This guide explains the main specifications to check before purchasing a rebar threading machine and how to select the right configuration. What Is a Rebar Threading Machine? A rebar threading machine is used to produce an external thread on the prepared end of a reinforcement bar. The threaded bar is then connected to a compatible mechanical coupler. Depending on the machine design, threading may be performed through thread rolling or thread chasing . Roll-threading systems use dies or rollers to form the thread, while chaser systems use cutting tools to produce the thread profile. The complete process generally involves: TMT bar → end preparation → threading → inspection → coupler connection Mechanical couplers are covered by IS 16172:2023 , which specifies requirements and tests for reinforcement couplers used for mechanical splicing of reinforcement bars conforming to IS 1786. BIS identifies several coupler types, including parallel threaded, upset parallel threaded, tapered threaded, crimped sleeve, injected sleeve and shear-bolting systems. Why Is Machine Selection Important? A threading machine that does not match the project’s reinforcement requirements can create problems such as: Incorrect thread dimensions Inadequate thread length Poor thread profile Difficult coupler engagement Increased tool wear Lower production output Unnecessary power consumption Higher maintenance requirements Rework during reinforcement fabrication The correct machine should therefore be selected based on the complete mechanical splicing system , not on the machine specification alone. 1. Check Rebar Diameter Capacity The first specification to check is the rebar diameter range . For example, a machine designed for 16–40 mm reinforcement bars is intended to process bars within that specified range. Several machines available in the Indian market use a 16–40 mm capacity, although other configurations are available. Before buying, check: Minimum bar diameter Maximum bar diameter Actual TMT sizes used on the project Required thread diameter Compatibility with the selected coupler Availability of suitable dies or rollers Press enter or click to view image in full size Example If your project primarily uses: 16 mm 20 mm 25 mm 32 mm 36 mm 40 mm then a 16–40 mm machine can cover the complete stated diameter range, provided the machine’s tooling and threading system are designed for those sizes. Do not select capacity only from the maximum diameter. The machine must perform consistently across the sizes that you process most frequently. 2. Understand Thread Length Thread length is another important specification. A machine may have an advertised maximum threading length of 80 mm, 100 mm or another value depending on its design. For example, CDRG-45 listings commonly specify an 80 mm maximum threading length , while some other machines list longer capacities. The required thread length should be determined by the coupler design and approved connection system . Do not select a machine simply because it has a longer thread length. Instead, confirm: Required thread engagement Coupler manufacturer’s specification Thread profile Bar diameter Thread pitch Required preparation length Project specification A longer thread is not automatically a better connection. The thread must be compatible with the coupler for which the bar is being prepared. 3. Check Motor Power Motor power affects the machine’s ability to process reinforcement bars and maintain production performance. Machines available in the market can have different motor ratings depending on their capacity and threading technology. Examples include machines around 5 HP , 4 kW , 5.5 kW and higher configurations. Press enter or click to view image in full size When comparing motor power, consider: Maximum rebar diameter Threading method Production volume Number of bars processed per shift Frequency of operation Electrical supply available at the site Machine duty cycle A higher horsepower rating alone does not guarantee better threading quality. The motor, gearbox, spindle, dies/rollers, machine frame and threading mechanism must work together. 4. Check Electrical Requirements Before purchasing, confirm that the machine can be operated with the electrical supply available at your fabrication yard or construction site. Com
